'''Geneviève Guitel''' (24 May 1895 &ndash; 30 July 1982) was a French mathematician. Post retirement, she had a second career as a historian of mathematics. She is noted for her work on the history of [[Numeral system|numeral systems]]. While working as a teacher in a Paris lycée, she undertook independent research into [[algebraic geometry]], specifically [[Hosohedron|trihedrons]] and [[Tetrahedron|tetrahedrons]], and explored [[Polygon|polygons]] and [[number theory]].<ref name=":1" /> She is remembered for introducing the terms [[long and short scales]] to refer to two of the main numbering systems used around the world. 

== Life ==

=== Early life and education ===
Geneviève Guitel was born in [[Marly-le-Roi]] on 24 May 1895. She was a niece of French historian [[Charles Bémont]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Fonds Geneviève Guitel et Charles Morazé |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/?url=https://archives.humatheque-condorcet.fr/archive/fonds/FRCC_34491 |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=archive.wikiwix.com}}</ref> She studied at the Faculty of Science at the [[University of Rennes]], and in 1920 placed first in a women's mathematics competitive examination, the [[agrégation]].<ref name=":0">[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-02-28</ref>

=== Career in mathematics ===
[[File:Lycée_Molière,_71_rue_du_Ranelagh,_Paris_16e.jpg|thumb|[[Lycée Molière (Paris)|Lycée Molière]], 71 rue du Ranelagh, Paris]]
Guitel was appointed as mathematics teacher in 1920<ref>[http://rhe.ish-lyon.cnrs.fr/?q=agregsecondaire André Chervel, "Les agrégés de l’enseignement secondaire. Répertoire 1809-1950"]</ref> working first in Rennes, then Neuilly, before moving to teach at the [[Lycée Molière (Paris)|Lycée Molière]], a secondary school in Paris in 1936, eventually becoming a professor there.<ref name="Académie">{{cite web
| title = ''Comptes rendus hebdomadaires des séances de l'Académie des sciences'', séance du 5 décembre 1955, vol.241, p.1658 
| url   = https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k31937/f1664
}}</ref> Whilst working there, Guitel undertook independent research. She studied [[algebraic geometry]], specifically [[Hosohedron|trihedrons]] and [[Tetrahedron|tetrahedrons]], as well as exploring [[Polygon|polygons]] and [[number theory]].<ref name=":1" /> She published mathematical papers between 1943–1979.<ref>http://www.centre-charles-moraze.msh-paris.fr/IMG/pdf/moz17-4.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022193509/http://www.centre-charles-moraze.msh-paris.fr/IMG/pdf/moz17-4.pdf |date=22 October 2013 }} pp 474–475. {{in lang|fr}}</ref> 

In 1953, Guitel defended her [[State doctorate|state doctoral]] thesis on the metric study of [[tetrahedron]] families.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Geneviève Guitel - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=290660 |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]}}</ref> 

=== Career in history of mathematics ===
Guitel retired from the [[:fr:Lycée Molière (Paris)|Lycée Molière]] in 1960 but continued her research through a contract at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) exploring the history of [[Numeral system|numeral systems]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-11 |title=72 femmes scientifiques, dont 11 mathématiciennes d’exception, bientôt inscrites sur la Tour Eiffel ! {{!}} CNRS Mathématiques |url=https://www.insmi.cnrs.fr/fr/cnrsinfo/72-femmes-scientifiques-dont-11-mathematiciennes-exception-bientot-sur-tour-eiffel |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=www.insmi.cnrs.fr |language=fr}}</ref> This research was supported by the French historian and economist {{Ill|Charles Morazé|fr}}, who Guitel had first met in 1949. She became close to the Morazé family whilst working in collaboration with Charles and historian [[Fernand Braudel]]. The men were co-founders of the ''[[School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences|Sixième section]]''  at the ''[[École pratique des hautes études]]'' (EPHE). She had known Braudel since the 1930s when she was working at the Lycée Molière, her uncle Charles Bémont having been one of his mentors.<ref name=":1" /> Guitel was part of Morazé’s research seminars at the Sixth Section until 1975, researching and publishing a number of articles on the history of mathematics in the journal [[Annales school|''Les Annales'']].<ref name=":1" />

In 1975, she published a book ''Histoire comparée des numérations écrites'', (Comparative History of Written Number Systems) where on p. 51–52 and in the chapter "Les grands nombres en numération parlée", p. 566–574, (English: The large numbers in oral numeration) she first recorded use of the terms [[long and short scales]] (''échelle longue'' and ''échelle courte'').<ref>{{cite book
  | last = Guitel
  | first = Geneviève 
  | title = Histoire comparée des numérations écrites
  | publisher = Flammarion
  | language = French
  | year = 1975
  | location = Paris
  | pages = 51–52
  }}</ref><ref>{{cite book
  | last = Guitel
  | first = Geneviève 
  | title = Histoire comparée des numérations écrites
  | publisher = Flammarion
  | language = French
  | year = 1975
  | location = Paris
  | pages = 566–574 – chapter "Les grands nombres en numération parlée" (English: The large numbers in oral numeration)
  }}</ref> Afterwards, she resigned from her research fellowship the same year, aged 80.<ref name=":1" />

== Honors and awards ==
In 1955, she was awarded the [[French Academy of Sciences]]' {{ill|Gegner prize|fr|Prix Gegner de l'Académie des sciences}} for her doctoral thesis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Académie des sciences |first=(France) |date=1955-07-01 |title=Comptes rendus hebdomadaires des séances de l'Académie des sciences / publiés... par MM. les secrétaires perpétuels |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k31937 |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=Gallica |language=EN}}</ref> She was only the second woman to be awarded the prize, the first female recipient was [[Marie Curie]].

In 2026, Guitel was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-05 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Archive ==
Guitel made the Morazé family her sole legatees and left them her papers, which were later donated to the library of the [[University of Technology of Compiègne]] following Charles Morazé's death, along with his archives.<ref name=":1" />
